title: 2021-05-06 DevOps and Core discuss testing
content:
Attendees:

Background

As a part of the greater IPEX journey towards an organisation embracing the DevOps culture we set up a meeting with the Core team to learn from them with a focus on testing and automating.

Notes

The core team currently has four types of automated testing:

  • Unit testing

    • The responsibility on writing these lie on the developer.

      • The culture within the team and the structure of the system should allow for this

      • The team has admittedly elected to not focus as much on unit test currently due to the ease of running integration tests.

  • Integration tests in Kotlin

    • The responsilibity lies on the team

    • The team has focused on building an extensive suite

  • Integration tests in JavaScript & TypeScript

    • This requires buy-in from Product Owner

      • This work is more extensive and requires plenty of time set aside during work to ensure that this is done.

  • Generate documentation with working code examples

    • Core uses a tool called Orchid to generate documentation.

      • Orchid allows the team to tag their code base to extract working code into the documentation. Automatically updates when code changes.

    • Kompis has their own built solution for generating documentation, DevOps team will reach out to

  • Api tests - Tests in js/ts that verify api, a failure of one of these signals that an api changed in a way that needs to be documented as a breaking change.

The Core team suggest the following “1000%ers” that would be a good place to start for teams:

  • Introduce a pull-request process that remind the developer to provide tests and code for the newly introduced code

    • My note: Introducing it from now and moving forward would improve the testability and quality of the system no matter the previous state. Initial investment should be investigated by the team.

  • Introduce document generation for the code with examples.

Additional thoughts and ideas:

Core has a pipeline that submits a pull request for the PAX planner to update their Core version. This is a great way to increase adoption and make it easier for teams to upgrade. As part of the pull request pipeline a set of tests are run to ensure compatibility. In the ideal case, Core updates and a short while later the PAX planner can just accept the pull request and have the latest version of Core running.

Core is planning to use PlantUML to create sequence diagrams. This goes well in line with the architectural discussions relating to having diagrams for HLD and LLD available.

Wish list for future improvements

Look into using BDD tooling. Mikael has previously worked with Specflow.

Performance testing and setting up dashboards. Ola mentioned that there are a few plugins for Github that can be used to assist.

Sonarqube / Sonarcloud

Follow-up

A follow-up meeting has been scheduled for 2nd of June.
